keys.description: Completeness tier for the audit log. Higher tiers add forensic / analytics value at the cost of DB growth and supervisor-thread overhead.  decisions = only proxy-evaluated events (today's historical behaviour). spawns    = + a compact row for every routine ProcessSpawn short- circuit (find, grep, ls, base64, …). Answers "what binaries did this session execute?" with modest write volume. Default. io        = + compact rows for routine file reads / writes. Forensic- ish; ~+100 MB/day under typical dev workloads. all       = + compact rows for noise-path events (/proc/, /dev/null, /var/cache/, CA cert dirs, …). Best for compliance / SIEM exports; requires retention tuning (~+500 MB/day).  Compact rows omit filter_results / filter_scores / composite_score and carry only the call type, supervised pid + tool, and a short argument summary. The dashboard hides them by default; toggle "Show routine activity" on the audit page to reveal them.
keys.name: completeness

keys.description: set to false to keep audit records local-only; license checks still use grith.ai
keys.name: audit_sync

keys.description: "community", "pro", or "enterprise"
keys.name: plan_tier

keys.description: auto-deny queued calls after 5 minutes
keys.name: review_timeout_seconds

keys.description: Work item 68: destructive-action coverage. Hard-denies catastrophic host/storage destruction (mkfs, dd-to-device, wipefs, rm --no-preserve-root, recursive removal of a system root or database data directory) and escalates destructive operations directed at production (prod DB endpoints, or prod/production/live-tagged resources) from QUEUE to DENY. Non-production destructive ops QUEUE; scoped dev operations (rm -rf of project dirs, single-object staging deletes, read-only queries) are not flagged. ON by default — this is the coverage behind grith's "blocks the destructive step" claim. Set false to disable the whole filter.
keys.name: enabled

keys.description: Stub in v1.5, requires local embedding model
keys.name: enabled

keys.description: Gate the rate-limit filter's volume penalties (burst/per-minute/approaching) on per-op risk, so a burst of untainted routine file churn (~/.cache, .git/ internals, build outputs) never escalates. The supervisor's target-aware mass-destruction signal backfills the one case this drops (an untainted destructive spree). See work/futurework/rate-limit-burst-redesign.md.  ON by default (rollout step 4). Setting this false restores the legacy frequency-blind burst counter and also forfeits the scratch/~/.cache/.git exemptions (retired in favour of this gate) — expect routine-churn prompts.
keys.name: risk_gated_burst

keys.description: Keep both spawn prompt-reduction signals off by default until operators review telemetry/profile inventory for their environment.
keys.name: routine_provenance_signal

keys.description: Data-flow taint-on-spawn (PR 2). Default ON (FP research §5.2): the legacy "any session taint → +3.0 on every spawn/connect" flagged read-credential-then-use-credential (~/.npmrc → npm, ~/.kube/config → kubectl). The data-flow rule still catches genuine exfil.
keys.name: taint_data_flow_only

keys.description: Narrow condition 4 of the data-flow taint rule (FP §5.2). When true, an outbound-capable binary under taint (`git push`, `aws s3 ls`, `npm publish`) only fires when the spawn actually references the tainted data (argv path/env, pipe/redirect, shell-pattern) — not merely because a credential was read earlier and the tool is outbound-capable. Genuine exfil still fires via conditions 1–3/5, and outbound-to-untrusted-destination is scored by egress. Set false to restore the standalone outbound-binary fire.
keys.name: taint_outbound_requires_data_flow

keys.description: Open the dashboard in your browser on startup, handing off the auth token via the URL fragment (never printed to the terminal). Auto-skipped on headless/SSH sessions. When false or unavailable, the CLI prints a single-use pairing URL instead. Override per-run with GRITH_AUTO_OPEN_DASHBOARD=0.
keys.name: auto_open_dashboard

keys.description: Linux attach mechanism: "traceme" (shipped) | "seize" (work in progress — selecting it currently aborts with a clear error). See work/futurework/ptrace-seize-migration.md.
keys.name: attach_mode

keys.description: Seconds to keep running after the daemon stops accounting for this session (it answered a heartbeat with "I am not tracking you" — usually because it restarted while at its session cap). 0 = never terminate: the session keeps running with a loud warning and you decide. Terminating by default would destroy in-progress agent work over a daemon-side event you did not cause. Set a positive value in CI, where nobody is watching the warning.
keys.name: authority_lost_terminate_after_seconds

keys.description: Decide D-Bus control-socket access per *method call* instead of per connection. At `connect(2)` there is nothing to judge but a socket path — "read the keyring" and "ask systemd to run this command outside supervision" are byte-identical syscalls — so enforcing there charges a prompt for every credential-helper lookup. With this on (the default), a connect to a D-Bus endpoint instead arms message inspection: grith decodes the calls the tool writes to that socket and escalates only the ones a curated allowlist does not vouch for. `gh auth token`'s keyring read stops prompting; `org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager.StartTransientUnit` still QUEUEs, and now says so by name.  Fails toward the old behaviour: an unreadable payload, an undecodable stream or an unlisted method escalates the connection exactly as enforce_control_socket_connect alone would. Only D-Bus is affected — X11, tmux and screen carry no per-message destination and keep connect-time enforcement. Has no effect when enforce_control_socket_connect is false. Emergency override: GRITH_DBUS_MESSAGE_INSPECTION=0 (or =1 to force on).
keys.name: dbus_message_inspection

keys.description: Enforce the authority-delegating-binary-spawn detection. When false, spawning systemd-run / at / docker / systemctl / dbus-send / … is detected and forensically logged but still allowed (audit-only). When true (the default since v0.2.5), such a spawn is escalated Allow→QUEUE for review unless the profile's permit_authority_delegating list names the binary — closing the `systemd-run --user … -- <cmd>` supervision escape (the command's effect runs in a peer OUTSIDE the supervised tree, where nothing it does is intercepted). Escalation is QUEUE, not deny, so you can approve legitimate use once (the approval sticks for the session, and read-only subcommands like `docker ps` never prompt); a non-interactive session fails safe (denies) — set this false or use the profile permit list for unattended/CI sessions that legitimately delegate. Emergency override: GRITH_ENFORCE_AUTHORITY_DELEGATING_SPAWN=1 (or =0 to force off).
keys.name: enforce_authority_delegating_spawn

keys.description: Enforce the control-injection-IPC-socket-connect detection (session D-Bus, tmux, screen, X11). When false such a connect is audit-only (auto-allowed as local IPC). When true (the default since v0.2.5) it is routed to the proxy and escalated Allow→QUEUE unless the profile's permit_control_sockets list authorises it. Independent knob — desktop tooling touches the session bus routinely, so this has a higher false-positive surface than the spawn flag. Abstract-namespace sockets (the kind X11 clients try first) ARE matched — they render as `unix:@<name>` and classify like any other path. Emergency override: GRITH_ENFORCE_CONTROL_SOCKET_CONNECT=1 (or =0 to force off).
keys.name: enforce_control_socket_connect

keys.description: H2 Option 1 (IPC-delegated authority): enforce PTY ownership. When false (default), writes to a /dev/pts/N that is NOT the supervised tool's own controlling terminal are detected and forensically logged (event = "foreign_pts_write") but still allowed — audit-only, to measure the false-positive budget. Set true to DENY them (the `echo cmd > /dev/pts/<other pane>` IPC-injection vector). See work/futurework/ipc-delegated-authority-escape.md.
keys.name: pty_ownership_enforce

keys.description: A proxy-owned upstream socket can have network access the tracee lacks due to cgroups, firewall owner rules, SO_MARK/SO_BINDTODEVICE, or policy routing. Set true only after that authority difference is explicitly reviewed and accepted or equivalently contained. The proxy refuses to start otherwise.
keys.name: accept_proxy_network_authority

keys.description: Deny TCP-DNS, forcing resolution onto the inspected UDP path. TCP-DNS can't be content-inspected (its query/response ride write()/read(), the hottest syscalls, deliberately not intercepted), so leaving it enabled would let a tool bypass query blocking over TCP. The rare cost is a lookup whose answer exceeds EDNS0-UDP size failing (modern resolvers use EDNS0 UDP up to 4 KB, so TCP fallback is seldom needed); such a case surfaces as a visible deny. Set false to allow TCP-DNS uninspected. Default on.
keys.name: block_tcp_dns

keys.description: Canary path for connected UDP/53 sockets whose query/response use plain write()/read() and are therefore invisible to in-line inspection. Off until the Phase 0 resolver, namespace, race, lifecycle, and performance gates pass.
keys.name: connected_udp_proxy

keys.description: In-line DNS inspection (Linux). Discovers connected and unconnected UDP DNS destinations, parses every sendto/sendmsg/sendmmsg query before send, and lets allowed queries reach the machine's real resolver untouched. Malformed port-53 payloads fail closed. DoT (port 853) is denied.
keys.name: enabled

keys.description: Observe DNS responses to populate the exact IP->domain cache the egress / reputation filters use. This promotes tracked recvfrom/recvmsg/recvmmsg calls to catch their exits (one tightly-scoped PTRACE_SYSCALL step per DNS receive). Query blocking does not depend on this. Default on.
keys.name: observe_responses

keys.description: Bound the proxy data plane. Oversized responses fail explicitly rather than being silently truncated.
keys.name: proxy_max_response_bytes

keys.description: QUEUE-range policy decisions from either DNS inspection owner (the in-line sendto/sendmsg path and the connected-UDP proxy) enqueue review but refuse the current lookup. "forward" is an explicit compatibility mode which permits DNS before review and must not be used for complete-enforcement claims.
keys.name: proxy_queue_action

keys.description: Bounds route-task draining; the owning thread is always joined afterward.
keys.name: proxy_shutdown_timeout_ms

keys.description: Extra project roots to trust, for layouts git cannot infer — a worktree of a DIFFERENT repository parked alongside this one, or a non-git sibling checkout. `${HOME}`, `${PROJECT_DIR}` and `~` expand as in routine_paths. Every root is canonicalised, and `/`, your home directory and any ancestor of it are refused. At most 32 roots are trusted per session.  Trust here is project-derived, never literal: credential stores (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .npmrc, …) inside a trusted root still go to the security proxy.
keys.name: additional_project_roots

keys.description: How far this session's project trust reaches. `${PROJECT_DIR}` in a profile's routine_paths expands to the LAUNCH DIRECTORY only, so in a multi-worktree layout the sibling worktrees of the repository you are working on get no trust at all — measured 24.9% of calls prompting there against 0.32% under the launch directory, and one `git worktree remove` producing 692 bulk-delete prompts.  Trust every git worktree of the launch repository. `git worktree list` reports the main worktree too, so launching from a subdirectory also trusts the repository root (a tool working in `repo/frontend/` stops prompting on every read of `../package.json`). Resolved once, at session start, and never re-read: a re-read would let the supervised tool widen its own trust with `git worktree add`.
keys.name: include_linked_worktrees

keys.description: Make the workspace a wall instead of a trusted island. With this on, a file read or write whose target is outside the workspace (the launch directory, its linked git worktrees, and additional_project_roots above) is DENIED rather than scored — including the read-only opens that noise_reduction.ignore_read_only waves through today. Your other projects, the rest of your home directory, mounted media: none of them are readable.  What stays reachable, because the tool cannot run otherwise: system runtime paths for READS only (/usr, /lib, /bin, /etc, …), grith's noise paths (/proc, /sys, the terminal), and the paths the tool's own profile declares as routine (~/.claude, ~/.nvm/versions/**, /tmp/<tool>-*, …).  This only ever removes access. It cannot allow anything the proxy would otherwise block — a read of /etc/shadow is still denied by the filters. Filesystem only: network and process spawn are unaffected.  Per session: `grith exec --workspace-only -- <tool>`.
keys.name: restrict_to_workspace
